newsitem.title: USA: Freighter aground in marine sanctuary off Florida.
newsitem.headline: Freighter aground in marine sanctuary off Florida.

text.p: A container ship on its way to Spain from New Orleans apparently lost its way on Monday and ended up in a fragile marine sanctuary south of the Florida Keys, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

Petty Officer Jeff Hall, a Coast Guard spokesman, said the 600-foot (200-meter) Liberian-flagged Houston had run aground about 12 miles (19 km) southeast of Key West at 5:30 a.m. EST (1030 GMT) and remained stuck in the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, a 120-mile (193-km) protected area surrounding the small islands on Florida's south end.
It had not yet been determined what damage the ship might have done but it might have smashed some of the delicate coral reefs as it travelled to the spot where it ran aground.
"It is on a sandy coral bottom so it is probably not on a reef right now," Hall said. "But who knows what it went through to get there?"
A freighter bound for Europe from New Orleans typically would have been far out to sea while passing Florida.

The freighter was carrying general cargo, meaning that any fuel and lube oil on board was its only potentially hazardous cargo. Emergency teams were checking the ship to make sure there were no holes in its hull before moving it.
Hall said the Coast Guard hoped to be able to float the ship at high tide at 6 p.m. EST (2300 GMT) but keeping to that timetable could be difficult.
He said he did not know who owned the ship or why it was off its course.
